Subject: Re: ACTION: PH P0 — triage notes and recommended mitigations

Connor / team — initial triage:
- Symptoms line up with a prefill/backpressure scenario on the tokenizer service causing GPU workers in us-west-2 to back up; requests time out and return 502/503.
- Memory pressure observed on the host pool serving redwood-gpt-7b-quant (OOM-kill attempts recorded in node logs).

Short-term mitigations we can execute immediately (requires ops routing change):
1) Canary redirect 10% of traffic to us-west-1 (same model variant) and warm KV caches. Monitor per-token latency and 5xx.
2) If stable at 10% for 5 minutes, step to 50%.
3) If we see continued memory pressure we will fallback to a quantized-lowmem variant (redwood-gpt-7b-q4) in us-east-1 for additional capacity.

Estimate: 30–45 minutes to stabilize traffic at 50% if canary passes. Risk: small disruption to in-flight requests during steering; model fallback may change token-level quality marginally.

I'm ready to run the steering once commercial/exec sign-off on emergency burst capacity and credit is OK.

Hannah
SRE Lead, Runtime Reliability

- If switching to q4 variant, we expect ~40% lower memory usage per shard which should remove the immediate OOM pressure. Expected latency delta: +30–70ms token-level on average.
- Emergency reserved burst: we can allocate up to 8 GPUs in us-east-1 from the emergency pool for up to 6 hours. Estimated incremental cost: $3,800 for 6 hours (emergency pricing).

Requesting:
1) Commercial approval to use emergency pool (cost above) and pre-authorize a one-time credit for the customer to offset impact during the incident.
2) Exec acknowledgement of the quality tradeoff if we fall back to q4 model.

Marcus
